ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, wooden block A has a mass of 1kg, and wooden block B has a mass of 2kg. They are stacked on horizontal ground. The maximum static friction force between A and B is 1N, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between B and the ground is 0.1. Now a horizontal force F is applied to B. If A and B are to be kept relatively at rest, what is the maximum value of F? (g=10m/s^2)
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, wooden block A is stacked above wooden block B, and wooden block B is placed on horizontal ground indicated with diagonal lines; the horizontal force F acts on the lower wooden block B, in the direction to the right. Then reason: It is known that m_A=1kg, m_B=2kg, the maximum static friction force between A and B is 1N, the coefficient of kinetic friction between B and the ground is μ=0.1, and g=10m/s². If A and B remain relatively at rest, A can only obtain horizontal acceleration by means of the static friction force between A and B, so A's maximum allowable acceleration satisfies f_max=m_A a_max, namely a_max=1/1=1m/s². Treat A and B as a whole; the magnitude of the friction force of the ground on B is μ(m_A+m_B)g=0.1×3×10=3N, and its direction is opposite to the tendency of motion. Apply Newton's second law to the whole: F-3=(m_A+m_B)a=3a. Taking the critical a=1m/s², we get F_max-3=3×1, so F_max=6N.
